description: AION 2 game mechanics the Ascent Plan rests on, one record per rule with a status. confirmed: seen in game or settled by Miguel. unconfirmed: guides say it, nobody has tested it yet; every page that rests on it shows a Not confirmed yet tag and the in-game test below. Flip a status here and every screen follows. Sources stay in this file, never on a page. The macro facts themselves (slots, delay, hold, interrupt, key binding) live in progression.json under macro-order; the macro-order rule here points at them so there is one place to edit.

records.label: Skill stacks
records.text: Each key holds up to four skills stacked in rows 0 to 3, row 0 nearest the key. Pressing the key checks row 0 first: if that skill is ready it fires, otherwise the game moves up to row 1, 2 and 3 and fires the first one that is ready.
rules: Cooldown skills at the bottom, no-cooldown filler at the top.
A no-cooldown skill below a cooldown skill blocks it: it is always ready, so the key never reaches the skill above.
Heals, defensives, big buffs and charged skills go on their own keys, so you choose when they fire.

sources.note: Screenshot of his own bar: four rows on a key, row 0 at the bottom, the key fires the lowest ready skill.

records.label: Chain skills
records.text: Using some skills opens a follow-up skill for a short window. The skill tooltip lists the skills that lead into a follow-up.
records.unknown: How the follow-up is pressed and how long the window lasts are not confirmed.
records.test: Use a lead-in skill, then press the follow-up's key at once. Does it fire, and how long is it available?

leadIns.reason: The tooltip names two lead-in skills. They are not captured yet.

records.label: How a macro fires
records.text: Guides disagree on how a macro picks its next skill.

options.text: The macro runs its entries in the listed order, 1 then 2 and so on.
The macro works like a stack: it fires the first ready entry from the bottom and skips entries on cooldown.

notes: Adding a stacked key to a macro runs that key's stack.
Holding left click with the macro key makes it cycle faster (guides, not tested).
records.test: Make a macro with A then B, and get A on cooldown. Does B fire, and when A is ready again does the macro go back to A first?
